flaw.code_asserting_copy_eq_copy: assert json.loads(BASELINE_GAPS_PATH.read_text()) == BASELINE_GAPS, ("U8.15 baseline on disk disagrees with the inline frozen copy")
flaw.why_it_cannot_detect_transcription_error: It compares two DERIVED artifacts -- the inline dict and the JSON file -- and never either one against the measurement they both claim to record. Two copies of a wrong value agree perfectly, so a transcription slip is satisfied by the assertion: a slip in the inline dict reads as 'the file disagrees' in the other direction, and a slip that was copied into both is agreed to by both. U8.22's V6E.json under-declaration is exactly that class of error. The identical shape recurred at line 233 (recorded['contract_verifier'] == VERIFIER_CONTRACT) and line 234 (recorded['gaps'] == VERIFIER_BASELINE_GAPS), and in purest form at line 236 (set(BASELINE_NO_STATUSISH) == set(BASELINE_NO_STATUSISH_FROZEN), whose right-hand side was frozenset(BASELINE_NO_STATUSISH): a value compared with a copy of itself, so it can never fail).

design.chosen: single-source + hash-pin (recommended (a)+(b)), plus a tightening-only re-derivation (c) of the OVER-declaration direction
design.justification: The duplication is the hazard, so it is removed: each baseline JSON is now the sole source (no inline copy exists to compare against, and the verifier contract is read from the pinned record instead of being duplicated as a constant). Removing the copy would leave the file with no integrity check at all, so (b) is added to BOTH files -- U8.15's was already pinned, U8.18's was not. The pin makes a repair and a transcription slip the same kind of act: a visible change to two places (the file plus the pin), with a silent single-place change failing the suite. Rewriting the baseline from live data (the naive form of (c)) is REJECTED: it would re-absolve every recorded gap on every run -- a tautology that stops catching anything. What is re-derived is only the tightening direction: test_no_baseline_entry_over_declares re-measures the corpus and fails when an exemption claims MORE than the handoffs need (V5.25.json and U8.15's 41 dead V* entries were exactly this). That check cannot be vacuously satisfied by re-deriving the baseline because the baseline stays a pinned file while the measurement comes from disk, so the two can disagree -- and did.
design.what_it_proves: A silent transcription slip into either baseline is impossible (any byte change fails the pin, including a semantically neutral byte). A deliberate one requires editing the file AND the pin: two visible acts, which is the design goal. A stale or over-declared exemption that would hide a now-fixed handoff is caught by measurement. New/worsened gaps in the live corpus are still compared against the frozen records (test_no_new_contract_key_gaps), so the guard still catches a newly incomplete handoff of either shape.
design.what_it_does_not_prove: That the frozen exemptions were CORRECT when U8.15/U8.18 recorded them -- that historical measurement is relied on, not re-derived (deliberately). It does not prove a handoff's content is truthful, only that it parses and carries its contracted keys. It does not make a determined editor's change impossible, only visible and deliberate (file + pin + contract would all have to move together). And with the dead V* entries retired, the unit baseline holds only 4 entries, so it proves nothing about V* files -- by construction classify() never routes them there; the U8.18 record governs them.

loose_ends.v525_over_declaration: REMOVED. Before: "V5.25.json": ["next_unit_hint"]. After: the entry is deleted (5 verifier entries remain) and a revised_by/revised note inside the pinned file records why. Reason: live measurement is [] because that handoff now carries next_unit_hint; an exemption the corpus no longer needs is not harmless -- it would silently tolerate the handoff LOSING the key again. Retiring it makes a future loss a loud NEW gap again. Because the file is pinned, the retirement was a deliberate two-place change (file + pin), which is the design working as intended.
loose_ends.u815_dead_v_entries: RETIRED. 41 V*-prefixed entries removed from state/logs/U8.15/baseline_gaps.json (46 entries before, 4 unit entries after), documented in the file's retired_dead_v_entries note. Reason: classify() returns 'verifier' for ANY basename starting with 'V', so those unit-shaped key lists could never be consulted -- dead text that a future reader would take for enforced gaps (and they were measured stale besides: every key they listed is present in those files now). The 4 non-V entries are untouched, and no verifier gap is lost: V2T/V4R/V5F/V6E/V6F live in the U8.18 record and were re-measured live as correct.
loose_ends.why_not_vacuous: From the code: test_no_new_contract_key_gaps partitions audit()'s gaps by shape and calls _regressions(unit_gaps, shapes, BASELINE_GAPS_read_from_the_pinned_file). _regressions flags (i) any file ABSENT from the baseline as 'new' and (ii) any measured key beyond the frozen list as 'worsened'. Retiring the V* entries removes only entries that could never appear in unit_gaps (the shape partition excludes them), so the remaining 4 entries plus the new-file rule are unchanged in force. Demonstrated by the new fixture test test_unit_shape_baseline_still_catches_new_gaps: an unknown U9.99.json is reported as new with its full 5-key gap, and a U0.22.json wider than the frozen entry is reported as worsened (['artifacts','evidence']). A check with a SHORT baseline still catches new gaps because the catching power comes from the live corpus, not from the baseline's size; conversely an emptied baseline cannot be used to weaken the guard silently, because every formerly exempted gap would immediately fail as NEW (and the pin test asserts both maps are non-empty).

hand_ups.concurrency_finding: The guard's mid-write rule re-reads only IMMEDIATELY after a parse failure. A writer that pauses more than an instant (e.g. composing a large handoff in chunks) is indistinguishable from a committed broken file, so orchestration/handoffs/U6.23.json produced a genuine-looking hard failure for ~2 minutes (15980 bytes, stable across reads, error at EOF) before it was completed by its owner. That is the guard behaving as designed -- truncation is a real defect -- but it means the suite can legitimately be red while several units are writing. Do NOT 'fix' this with mtime windows or a retry loop; the docstring already rejects mtime windows for the same reason (a file that is old-but-broken must still be caught). The operational answer is that units write their handoff LAST and in one call.
